assessment: The incumbent already produces usable exports with seven-minute median handling for 24 unchanged-assignment files, supporting retention of its private, center-scoped CSV path. Overall intended-course coverage was 32/40 (80%) and median handling 17 minutes. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports but do not establish causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Short job execution and long replacement waits suggest a separate coordination delay, whose cause is unmeasured. Zero observed cross-center rows does not establish isolation for the omitted split-course center. Coordinator checking and spreadsheet import costs remain unobserved.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may exclude intended courses; week-relevant selection could reduce assignment-associated corrections.
openings.delta: Locate a possible error in course selection before changing the scheduler or CSV format.
openings.prediction: With identical fabricated attendance and requested week, changing only the current assignment changes incumbent course inclusion; a week-relevant rule retains the coordinator-agreed course set.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare unchanged and midweek-transfer fixtures, then a split-course fixture with distinct center assignments. Agree expected sets with coordinators first. Compare course membership and center ownership under current and candidate rules while attendance entry continues. Preserve the documented CSV schema; estimate implementation within six engineer-days and existing hosting before choosing a change.
assumptions: Week-relevant membership can be defined unambiguously.
Historical assignment data availability is unknown; fabricated fixtures test behavior, not production feasibility.

openings.claim: Were renamed courses absent from the export, or present under names that failed coordinator reconciliation?
openings.delta: Distinguish selection failure from naming or timetable mismatch in the concrete counterexample to assignment-only repair.
openings.prediction: A reconciliation mismatch retains the expected internal course identity and participant rows but produces a missing-course report; selection failure lacks those rows before spreadsheet import.
openings.probe: Use fabricated rename cases in the six coordinators' short sessions. Compare internal course identities with agreed intended sets and observe checking and import separately. Keep the CSV unchanged and all participant material in private staging or authorized workspaces; bound this diagnostic before implementation.
assumptions: Fabricated sessions approximate real checking sufficiently to discriminate these mechanisms.
